headline: 146 goals in 234 games: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football
summary: The 41-year-old legend exits the Portugal national team with a record-breaking career, following a fall-out with coach Jorge Jesus.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo has officially retired from international football, ending a journey that began in August 2003. The 41-year-old confirmed the decision via social media on Thursday.
Ronaldo leaves as Portugal's leading goalscorer, having scored 146 goals in 234 appearances. His legacy includes leading the national team to victory in the 2016 European Championship.
The retirement comes amid reports of a fall-out with Portugal boss Jorge Jesus. The announcement was made just one day before the squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures was to be announced.
In an emotional farewell message, Ronaldo stated that football is about people and that he is proud to have represented Portugal for 23 years.
He expressed gratitude to his teammates, coaches, and staff, noting that while records are eventually broken, the passion for the country remains eternal.
The legendary forward leaves the national team with his head held high, having pushed beyond his limits to make history for his country.
caption:
146 goals, 234 appearances, and a European Championship title. The end of an era for Portugal.

Cristiano Ronaldo has officially retired from international football, ending a journey that began in August 2003. The 41-year-old confirmed the decision via social media on Thursday.

Ronaldo leaves as Portugal's leading goalscorer, having scored 146 goals in 234 appearances. His legacy includes leading the national team to victory in the 2016 European Championship.

The retirement comes amid reports of a fall-out with Portugal boss Jorge Jesus. The announcement was made just one day before the squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures was to be announced.

In an emotional farewell message, Ronaldo stated that football is about people and that he is proud to have represented Portugal for 23 years.

He expressed gratitude to his teammates, coaches, and staff, noting that while records are eventually broken, the passion for the country remains eternal.

The legendary forward leaves the national team with his head held high, having pushed beyond his limits to make history for his country.

headline: Ibrahim strike Bangladesh beat Bhutan 1-0 in SAFF opener
summary: A 69th-minute winner from substitute Mohammad Ibrahim secured a hard-fought victory for the hosts in their first match of the SAFF Championship 2026.
details: Substitute Mohammad Ibrahim scored the winning goal in the 69th minute, netting from close range after a deflection off a Bhutan defender.
The victory brought relief to 10,000 spectators at the National Stadium in Dhaka, as Bangladesh struggled to break down the lower-ranked Bhutanese side.
Head coach Thomas Dooley faced tactical questions after starting centre-back Bishwanath Ghosh as a lone striker, a decision that lacked the necessary finishing touch.
The team suffered an early setback when captain-designate Topu Barman was forced out of the starting XI due to a muscle injury during warm-ups.
Jamal Bhuyan captained the side in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Tariq Kazi and Quazem Shah Kirmanee filling in for the reshuffled lineup.
Bangladesh will now watch Bhutan play Sri Lanka on November 8 before facing the islanders themselves three days later.
In another opening match of the tournament, defending champions India defeated Pakistan 3-2 in a high-scoring encounter.
caption:
A late heroics from the bench! Mohammad Ibrahim's 69th-minute strike secures a narrow 1-0 win for Bangladesh against Bhutan.

Substitute Mohammad Ibrahim scored the winning goal in the 69th minute, netting from close range after a deflection off a Bhutan defender.

The victory brought relief to 10,000 spectators at the National Stadium in Dhaka, as Bangladesh struggled to break down the lower-ranked Bhutanese side.

Head coach Thomas Dooley faced tactical questions after starting centre-back Bishwanath Ghosh as a lone striker, a decision that lacked the necessary finishing touch.

The team suffered an early setback when captain-designate Topu Barman was forced out of the starting XI due to a muscle injury during warm-ups.

Jamal Bhuyan captained the side in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Tariq Kazi and Quazem Shah Kirmanee filling in for the reshuffled lineup.

Bangladesh will now watch Bhutan play Sri Lanka on November 8 before facing the islanders themselves three days later.

In another opening match of the tournament, defending champions India defeated Pakistan 3-2 in a high-scoring encounter.
